subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which Liberal Prime Minister disestablished the Church of Ireland in 1869?
questions.explain: Gladstone's first ministry disestablished the Church of Ireland in 1869 as part of his mission to 'pacify Ireland'.

questions.q: The Boundary Commission, intended to revise the Irish border, ultimately collapsed and the border was confirmed unchanged in which year?
questions.explain: The Boundary Commission's report was suppressed and the existing border confirmed by agreement in 1925.

questions.q: Daniel O'Connell's later mass campaign of the early 1840s aimed primarily at which objective?
options: Repeal of the Act of Union
Disestablishment of the Church of Ireland
questions.explain: O'Connell's 'monster meetings' of 1843 sought Repeal of the Union and restoration of an Irish parliament.

questions.q: In which year was the Anglo-Irish Treaty signed?
questions.explain: The Anglo-Irish Treaty was signed in London on 6 December 1921.

questions.q: Gladstone's Second Home Rule Bill of 1893 was passed by the Commons but defeated by which body?
questions.explain: The Second Home Rule Bill passed the Commons in 1893 but was rejected by the House of Lords.

questions.q: The Ulster unionist Solemn League and Covenant against Home Rule was signed in which year?
questions.explain: The Ulster Covenant was signed in September 1912 by hundreds of thousands pledging to resist Home Rule.

questions.q: Which Whig government's Treasury, dominated by laissez-faire principles, oversaw much of the Famine relief from 1846?
questions.explain: Lord John Russell's Whig government took office in 1846 and its laissez-faire approach, associated with Charles Trevelyan, shaped relief policy.

questions.q: Which Prime Minister championed the Act of Union but failed to secure the accompanying Catholic Emancipation he had implied?
questions.explain: Pitt the Younger drove the Union through but resigned in 1801 after George III refused to permit Catholic Emancipation.

questions.q: Which pro-Treaty leader and commander of the Free State army was killed in an ambush at Beal na Blath in 1922?
questions.explain: Michael Collins was killed at Beal na Blath, County Cork, in August 1922 during the Civil War.

questions.q: The Irish National Land League, agitating during the 'Land War', was founded in 1879 largely on the initiative of whom?
questions.explain: Michael Davitt founded the Land League in 1879, with Parnell as its president, to resist evictions and reduce rents.

questions.q: The Anglo-Irish Treaty of 1921 created the Irish Free State with what constitutional status?
options: A federal state with Northern Ireland
A self-governing dominion within the British Empire
questions.explain: The Treaty established the Irish Free State as a dominion, requiring an oath of allegiance to the Crown.

questions.q: Roughly how many people died during the Great Famine of 1845-49?
questions.explain: Approximately one million people died from starvation and disease during the Famine, with a further million emigrating.

questions.q: The Fenian Brotherhood / Irish Republican Brotherhood, founded in 1858, mounted an unsuccessful rising in which year?
questions.explain: The Fenian Rising occurred in 1867; its failure nonetheless kept physical-force republicanism alive.

questions.q: The Third Home Rule Bill reached the statute book in 1914 but its operation was suspended because of what?
options: The outbreak of the First World War
questions.explain: The Government of Ireland Act 1914 was placed on the statute book but suspended for the duration of the First World War.

questions.q: The Irish War of Independence (Anglo-Irish War) is generally dated from 1919 to which year?
questions.explain: The War of Independence ran from January 1919 until the truce of July 1921.

questions.q: The Irish Civil War over the Treaty was fought principally during which period?
questions.explain: The Civil War ran from June 1922 to May 1923, ending in victory for the pro-Treaty Free State forces.

questions.q: Sinn Fein's landslide in the December 1918 general election led to the establishment in 1919 of what body?
questions.explain: Sinn Fein MPs abstained from Westminster and constituted the First Dail Eireann in January 1919.

questions.q: Gladstone introduced his First Home Rule Bill in which year?
questions.explain: The First Home Rule Bill of 1886 was defeated in the Commons and split the Liberal Party.

questions.q: British policy after the Easter Rising, especially the execution of its leaders in May 1916, is generally seen by historians as having what effect?
questions.explain: The execution of sixteen leaders in 1916 generated sympathy and shifted public opinion towards radical separatism and Sinn Fein.

questions.q: Which unionist leader organised resistance to the Third Home Rule Bill and the Ulster Volunteer Force?
questions.explain: Sir Edward Carson led Ulster unionist opposition, with the UVF formed in 1913 to resist Home Rule by force if necessary.

questions.q: Sinn Fein was founded as a political movement in 1905 chiefly by whom?
questions.explain: Arthur Griffith founded Sinn Fein in 1905, initially advocating an Austro-Hungarian style dual monarchy rather than a republic.

questions.q: The proposed O'Connell 'monster meeting' that the government banned in 1843 was due to be held at which site?
questions.explain: The Clontarf meeting was banned in October 1843, and O'Connell's decision to call it off marked a decline in the Repeal movement.

questions.q: Who read the Proclamation of the Irish Republic outside the General Post Office during the Easter Rising?
questions.explain: Patrick Pearse, as president of the Provisional Government, read the Proclamation outside the GPO in 1916.

questions.q: Charles Stewart Parnell became leader of the Irish Parliamentary Party (Home Rule) in which year?
questions.explain: Parnell became chairman of the Irish Parliamentary Party in 1880, building it into a disciplined Home Rule bloc.

questions.q: In what year was the Act of Union, which abolished the Irish Parliament and created the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, passed?
questions.explain: The Act of Union was passed in 1800 and came into legal effect on 1 January 1801, merging the Kingdoms of Great Britain and Ireland.

questions.q: The Government of Ireland Act 1920 provided for partition by creating how many home-rule parliaments?
questions.explain: The 1920 Act created two parliaments, one for the six counties of Northern Ireland and one for Southern Ireland.

questions.q: In which year did the Easter Rising take place in Dublin?
questions.explain: The Easter Rising occurred in April 1916, when republicans seized buildings including the General Post Office.

questions.q: Whose election in the County Clare by-election of 1828 forced the Wellington government towards Catholic Emancipation?
questions.explain: Daniel O'Connell won the Clare by-election in 1828 but as a Catholic could not take his seat, precipitating Emancipation in 1829.

questions.q: The 'Young Ireland' rebellion, a short-lived rising during the Famine years, took place in which year?
questions.explain: The Young Ireland rising of 1848, often called the 'Battle of Widow McCormack's cabbage patch', was a minor affair in County Tipperary.

questions.q: Which Conservative Prime Minister repealed the Corn Laws in 1846 partly in response to the Irish Famine?
questions.explain: Robert Peel repealed the Corn Laws in 1846, splitting his party, partly to ease food supply during the Famine.
